attacks.claim: DPAs require all customer documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings, prompts) to be processed and stored in the EU. The plan puts retrieval in Nimbus Vector Store, which is provisioned in us-east-2 with EU only on a roadmap, so chunks and embeddings would be stored in the US from week 2.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap."

attacks.claim: Privileged legal document content, in the form of chunks and embeddings for 41M chunks, would be stored in a US region. The plan gives no transfer safeguards, subprocessor review, or tenant-data deletion on churn.
attacks.evidence: "currently provisioned in us-east-2" / ABSENT: transfer basis, subprocessor review, deletion on churn

attacks.claim: ZDR is documented only for the generation account addendum. The plan has no evidence that ZDR or EU residency covers embed-3 or the Vector Store. Embedding calls from ingest workers carry full document text.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." / ABSENT: ZDR or EU terms for embed-3 and Vector Store

attacks.claim: The agreed constraints make the 4,100-case regression suite the release gate for any model change. The plan defers it to week 6+, after the week 4 cutover, and justifies this with a 25-question blind comparison. This directly contradicts the constraint.
attacks.evidence: "so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: 25 questions from the support inbox cannot support a claim of quality parity across practice areas, long-context cases, or the behaviour previously provided by LoRA adapters. The preference result (19 of 25) is also too small to bound the regression rate.
attacks.evidence: "ran 25 representative questions from the support inbox through both stacks... This confirms quality parity or better"

attacks.claim: Week 3 releases the A100 reservation and deletes the fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters before the week 4 cutover and before any regression evaluation. If Nimbus fails on quality, latency, or compliance, the production model cannot be restored. This is a one-way door.
attacks.evidence: "release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: pgvector and the vLLM and GPU manifests are removed in week 5, before regression results exist in week 6+. Dual-write is described only for week 2, and no rollback or retirement criteria are given.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: The sequencing is inverted. Prompt tuning on failures happens after all tenants are already cut over. The week 2 re-embed and dual-write also has no backfill or consistency verification before cutover, and the embedding model changes so old and new vectors cannot be mixed.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks)... dual-write new documents." / "Week 6+: regression suite run, prompt tuning on any failures."

attacks.claim: The cost table ignores one-time re-embedding of 41M chunks and the parallel-run period. Generation is only an estimate. The savings claim is therefore unverified.
The plan moves to a single managed vendor for generation, embeddings, and retrieval, and deletes the weights and adapters needed to self-host again. It includes no exit or portability plan.
attacks.evidence: "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage to close out the 6.2 TB storage line"

attacks.claim: Production retrieval for all tenants would rely on a public-preview service. The plan does not address SLA, timeouts, retries, fallback, or alerting for the vendor dependency. The latency evidence covers only TTFT over a single week.
Tenant isolation through one collection and one scoped key per tenant has no described cross-tenant leakage testing or key audit. Rotation of keys for in-flight pods is also unspecified.
attacks.evidence: "one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key"

attacks.claim: Rate-limit headroom is 3x with no burst or quota alerting. The cost and latency of 200k-context requests are not modeled.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."
